rv.q: This production of For Colored Girls Who Have Considered Suicide When the Rainbow is Enuf is intense but theater is a great means of self-analysis.
At Fleetwood-Jourdain, Tim Rhoze directs and Marsae Lynette Mitchell choreographs a vibrant cast that makes Shange’s poetry sing.
Fleetwood-Jourdain’s revival of this play is a deserved recognition for the work of Ntozake Shange.
The production currently being featured at the Fleetwood-Jourdain Theatre and deftly directed by Tim Rhoze is taken from Shange’s updated version of the script from 2010.

cn.t: Critics praise this production of Shange's groundbreaking 1976 choreopoem, which powerfully addresses Black women's experiences of racism, sexism, and oppression through poetry, dance, and song rather than traditional plot.
